what: `.strip .term { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }` wraps every terminal with no hanging indent. The build command splits into lines that look like separate commands ('g++ -' / 'std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -g' / 'pass_three.cpp -o pass_three'), and 'anywhere' lets tokens break mid-word.
evidence: cpp-ch23.css:55; crops /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-21-25/a23/sheets/w390-00.png (p2: 'g++ -' then 'std=c++23' at column 0), w390-11.png (p26, p27). Compare the engine-wrapped terminals in the same chapter (p6 kennel_copy), which indent their continuation lines.
fix: Before: `.strip .term { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` → After: delete it, and add class="term wrap" only to the terminals whose key line is off-screen (why: the engine's .term.wrap gives continuation lines a hanging indent and protects caret lines; a blanket pre-wrap with anywhere does neither).

file: assets/comic.js (caretCol), seen in cpp/ch21.html P6, P12 and cpp/ch23.html P24
what: gcc's operand-range caret lines such as `|      ~ ^ ~~~~~` aren't recognised as caret lines, so in a .term.wrap/.wrap-sm terminal the source line above them isn't marked .tl-src and may wrap, and the carets drift under the wrong characters. These are the 'no match for operator+' and comparison errors the chapters read like a detective.
evidence: Probe (DOM): .tl lines not given tl-caret: ch21 member_plus.cpp '|                   ~ ^ ~~~~~', const_compare_bad.cpp '|            ~ ^  ~', ch23 array_assign.cpp '|     ~ ^'. The caretCol regex /^[\^~\-+]*\^[\^~\-+]*(?:\s|$)/ needs the markers to touch each other, and the gutter branch needs two or more '~' in a row, so 'tilde, space, caret' fails both.
fix: Before: `/^[\^~\-+]*\^[\^~\-+]*(?:\s|$)/.test(mk)` → After: `/^[\^~\-+]+(?: +[\^~\-+]+)*(?:\s|$)/.test(mk) && /\^/.test(mk)` (why: gcc puts spaces between the operand underlines and the operator caret).

panel: build-command lines of every wrapped terminal (e.g. ch22 P13, ch23 P17, ch24 P19)
what: Wrapped terminals break compiler flags at their hyphen ('g++ -' / 'std=c++23', '-fno-' / 'omit-frame-pointer'). The browser treats '-' as a break opportunity, although DESIGN_SYSTEM says terminal text 'breaks at spaces only'. A beginner copying the command sees `-` and `std=c++23` as separate pieces.
fix: Before: `.term.wrap .tl > .rest` text breaks at '-' → After: in comic.js paintTerm, wrap each space-free token in `<span class="tok-nb">` with `.tok-nb { white-space: nowrap }`, letting tokens longer than the line break with overflow-wrap (why: 'breaks at spaces only' as the design system promises; a flag must never split).
